title: Grill — dynamic model & effort catalog per harness
summary: **Round 3: two push-backs, then the grill is done.** One contradiction between two of your round-2 answers, and one edge case your Speed note opens.

questions.title: With no copilot on this machine, what happens to the copilot ACP probe?
questions.why: Your two round-2 answers can't both hold: the guard needs a live spike that stub-only rules out.
questions.context: Round 2 you chose **"Build from docs + stub fixtures only"** and also confirmed: *"If the copilot ACP spike shows that opening a session costs a premium request, writes copilot's own config, or doesn't list models with efforts, the probe is not shipped."* Without copilot installed, none of those three checks can run. The ACP spec tells us the *shape* a model/effort config option would have, but not whether copilot's server sends one, or what opening a session costs or writes.

options.label: Build it from the ACP spec, shipped switched off
options.description: Probe + parser + stub tests land, but copilot keeps `help config` by default. An env var (e.g. `AGETOR_COPILOT_ACP_DISCOVERY=1`) turns it on, and a later live check flips the default.
options.consequence: No unverified probe touches users; the code is ready for the live check.

options.label: Build it from the spec and ship it on
options.description: Any failure falls back to `help config`.
options.consequence: An unverified side effect (a paid request, a config write) could reach every copilot user.

options.label: Move copilot ACP out: a separate spike ticket
options.consequence: Copilot keeps `help config` in this change; nothing copilot-ACP is built.

options.label: I'll install and log in to copilot after all
options.consequence: The guard runs live, as confirmed in round 2.

recommendation.reason: Keeps your scope pick and your no-side-effect guard both true.

questions.title: Remembered Speed is Fast, and the new task's model can't do Fast. What happens to the remembered pick?
questions.why: Your note: "disable it if the new task chooses a model/harness that doesn't support fast mode… the same for efforts". The task falls back to Standard (or the model's default effort). Still open: whether the *remembered* pick survives.
questions.context: `lastSpeed:<kind>` already exists (cursor/fx), next to `lastModel`/`lastEffort`, all written when a task is submitted. Example: last task was Opus 5.5 + Fast. The next task picks Sonnet 5.5 (no fast mode), so it gets Standard. Then a third task picks Opus 5.5 again.

options.label: The memory stays Fast; it re-applies on the next Fast-capable model
options.description: Only an explicit pick changes the memory. Efforts work the same way: a remembered `xhigh` falls back to the model's default where unsupported and comes back where supported.
options.consequence: Third task is Fast again. A change from today: `lastSpeed`/`lastEffort` are written on submit, so today the fallback value overwrites the memory.

options.label: Falling back overwrites the memory with Standard
options.consequence: Third task is Standard; you re-pick Fast. This is how `lastSpeed:<kind>` / `lastEffort:<kind>` already behave for cursor/fx (written on submit, `NewTaskForm.tsx:689`).

recommendation.reason: A fallback isn't a choice you made, so it shouldn't erase the one you did make; it means writing the memory only on an explicit pick.
